Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: (noun) ini / itu (adjective). / (noun) ini tidak (adjective).

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Teh ini manis atau pahit? B: Manis.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Kopi ini pahit? B: Ya, pahit. Saya mahu gula.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Cili itu merah atau hijau? B: Cili itu hijau.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Bungkusan ini berat? B: Tidak, bungkusan ini ringan.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Pejabat encik besar? B: Tidak, pejabat saya sempit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: An adjective follows the noun and stands alone as the description: there is no word for "is". To say "not", put tidak in front of the adjective (tidak manis). bukan is for nouns (Ini bukan teh.). The adjective never changes.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：形容詞は名詞のあとに置き、そのまま述語になります。「〜は」にあたる語は要りません。否定は形容詞の前に tidak を置きます（tidak manis）。bukan は名詞用です（Ini bukan teh.）。形容詞の形は変わりません。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese i-adjectives and na-adjectives change form (辛い / 辛くない / 静かな); Malay has no such groups. pedas stays pedas; only tidak is added.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語のイ形容詞・ナ形容詞は形が変わります（辛い／辛くない／静かな）が、マレー語にはその区別がありません。pedas は pedas のままで、tidak を足すだけです。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: Pattern box: Bagaimana rasa ___ ? / ___ , tetapi ___ . (spoken: Macam mana, tapi)

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Bagaimana rasa mi goreng ini? B: Sedap, tetapi pedas.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Bagaimana rasa teh ini? B: Manis, tetapi sedap.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Bagaimana rasa mangga ini? B: Masam, tetapi segar.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Bagaimana rasa kopi ini? B: Pahit. Saya mahu gula.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 5. A: Macam mana? Sedap? (spoken) B: Sedap! Tetapi pedas sedikit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Explanation: Bagaimana rasa …? asks how something tastes. Answer with an adjective. tetapi joins two ideas that pull against each other; the second one is what you want to stress. sedikit after an adjective softens it: pedas sedikit. In speech, macam mana replaces bagaimana and tapi replaces tetapi.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 説明：Bagaimana rasa …? は味をたずねる表現で、形容詞で答えます。tetapi は反対の内容をつなぎ、あとに来る方が言いたいことです。形容詞のあとに sedikit を付けると和らぎます：pedas sedikit。話し言葉では bagaimana の代わりに macam mana、tetapi の代わりに tapi を使います。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the contrast on the first clause (辛いけどおいしい). Malay puts tetapi between the two: Pedas, tetapi sedap. Hear the order: the last idea wins.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は前の節に「けど」を付けます（辛いけどおいしい）。マレー語は二つの間に tetapi を置きます：Pedas, tetapi sedap. 最後に言う方が主役です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: Pattern box: Saya mahu ___ yang ___ . / ___ atau ___ ? (spoken: nak)

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 1. A: Encik mahu payung yang biru atau yang hitam? B: Saya mahu yang hitam.
target_spans: Encik mahu payung yang biru atau yang hitam?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 2. A: Puan mahu fail yang merah atau yang hijau? B: Yang hijau, ya.
target_spans: Puan mahu fail yang merah atau yang hijau?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 3. A: Encik mahu buku yang tebal atau yang nipis? B: Yang nipis.
target_spans: Encik mahu buku yang tebal atau yang nipis?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 4. A: Awak mahu mangga yang besar atau yang kecil? B: Yang besar. Berapa harga?
target_spans: Awak mahu mangga yang besar atau yang kecil?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 5. A: Panas atau sejuk? B: Sejuk.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Explanation: yang means "the one that is": yang biru is the blue one. Once everyone knows the noun you can drop it: Saya mahu yang hitam. atau offers a choice. mahu is "want"; in speech you will hear nak.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 説明：yang は「〜なもの」。yang biru は青いものです。相手が名詞を分かっていれば省けます：Saya mahu yang hitam. atau は選択肢を出します。mahu は「欲しい・〜したい」で、話し言葉では nak も聞きます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: yang biru works like the 青いの in 青いのをください: it points at one thing among several. For a plain description the bare adjective is enough (payung biru).

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 日本語との比較：yang biru は「青いのをください」の「青いの」に近く、いくつかの中から一つを指します。ただ描写するだけなら形容詞だけで十分です（payung biru）。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Pattern box: Saya rasa ___ . / Kenapa (= mengapa, apa sebab) ___ ? Sebab (or kerana) ___ .

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: 1. A: Encik rasa bagaimana hari ini? B: Saya rasa penat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: 2. A: Kenapa encik penat? B: Sebab semalam saya tidur lewat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: 3. A: Kenapa awak tidak makan? B: Sebab saya belum lapar.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|18.source_text: 4. A: Apa sebab bos marah? B: Sebab saya lambat.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|19.source_text: 5. A: Kenapa encik gembira? B: Sebab hari ini hari cuti.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|20.source_text: 6. A: Mengapa awak lambat? B: Kerana hujan.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Explanation: rasa before an adjective means "feel": Saya rasa penat. Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab all ask "why" and are interchangeable: kenapa is the everyday one. Answer with sebab or kerana, mainly; the reason follows the word.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 説明：形容詞の前の rasa は「感じる」：Saya rasa penat. Kenapa・mengapa・apa sebab はどれも「なぜ」で、言い換えられます（日常でよく使うのは kenapa）。答えは主に sebab か kerana で、理由はそのあとに続きます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the reason first and から after it (疲れたから). Malay does the reverse: Sebab (or kerana) comes first and the reason follows. kenapa ≈ どうして・なぜ; mengapa and apa sebab say the same thing.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は理由を先に言い、あとに「から」を付けます（疲れたから）。マレー語は逆で、Sebab（または kerana）が先に来て理由があとに続きます。kenapa ≈ どうして・なぜで、mengapa と apa sebab も同じ意味です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Pattern box: Saya mahu ___ , kurang manis, ais sedikit. / Panas atau sejuk?

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 1. A: Encik mahu minum apa? B: Saya mahu teh tarik, kurang manis.
target_spans: Saya mahu teh tarik, kurang manis.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 2. A: Panas atau sejuk? B: Sejuk. Ais sedikit.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 3. A: Makan sini atau tapau? B: Makan sini.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 4. A: Mi goreng ini pedas? B: Pedas sedikit, tetapi sedap.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 5. A: Ada apa lagi? B: Air kosong satu, ya.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: 6. A: Roti canai, dengan kuah? B: Ya, kuah banyak.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: Explanation: An order is built in a fixed order: the drink, how sweet it is, hot or cold, and how much ice. kurang manis is a fixed phrase for less sugar; use it only for ordering. air kosong is plain water.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|13.source_text: 説明：注文は決まった順番で組み立てます：飲み物、甘さ、温度（熱い・冷たい）、氷の量。kurang manis は砂糖控えめを頼む決まった言い方で、注文のときだけ使います。air kosong はお水です。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|14.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: It matches the way you customise a drink in Japan (甘さ控えめ、氷少なめ): same slots, same order. Do not build kurang into other sentences yet; comparing things comes in chapter 6.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|15.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本で飲み物をカスタムする言い方（甘さ控えめ、氷少なめ）と同じ項目・同じ順番です。kurang を他の文に広げるのは待ちましょう。比較は第6章で学びます。

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: Pattern 2: macam mana and tapi are spoken forms; accept them in pair work once bagaimana and tetapi have been practised.

Unit 5 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|4.source_text: Pattern 4: there is no Kata-Kata frame yet for Kenapa …? Sebab …; it is taught here with ms-c05-f04 (see the report). Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab are one question; accept sebab or kerana as the answer.

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: A mamak stall is a casual eatery, traditionally run by Indian-Muslim families and often open late, so it is also where people lepak and sembang after work. Use the word for the stall, not for a person. A drink order is built in a short sequence: the drink, how sweet it is, and hot or cold with a little ice: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit. The Kata-Kata scene and the ledger add the rest: makan sini or tapau (take away), Kira! for the bill, and roti canai dengan kuah (with gravy).
target_spans: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Drink names are short. Kata-Kata notes that teh O is tea without milk, and the ledger lists kopi O as black coffee with sugar, so kurang manis is how you ask for less sugar. Air kosong is plain water; Kata-Kata links kosong to the chapter 3 word for zero and empty.

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Colour words are easy to meet on the street. The national flag, the Jalur Gemilang, is red, white, blue and yellow: merah, putih, biru and kuning. Pink is merah jambu, literally "jambu-fruit red" (Kata-Kata card ms-c05-025). Yang lets you point at one thing among several: yang merah is "the red one" (card ms-c05-004).

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Malaysia is hot and humid throughout the year, so panas and sejuk are everyday words for the weather as well as for drinks. At the counter you will often hear nak for mahu (Saya nak teh tarik); Kata-Kata marks nak as spoken (card ms-c05-005).

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: mamak の店は気軽な食堂で、昔からインド系ムスリムの家族が営むことが多く、遅くまで開いていることもあるので、仕事のあとに lepak（ぶらぶらする）や sembang（おしゃべり）をする場所でもあります。この語は店に使い、人には使いません。飲み物の注文は、短い順番で組み立てます：飲み物、甘さ、熱い・冷たい、そして氷を少し：teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit。Kata-Kata の場面と台帳には、ほかに makan sini（店内で食べる）か tapau（持ち帰り）、お会計の Kira!、そして roti canai dengan kuah（カレーなどのたれ付き）があります。
target_spans: teh tarik, kurang manis, ais sedikit

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 飲み物の名前は短いです。Kata-Kata の注記では teh O はミルクなしの紅茶で、台帳では kopi O が砂糖入りのブラックコーヒーとされているので、砂糖を減らしたいときは kurang manis と言います。Air kosong はお水です。Kata-Kata は kosong を第3章の「ゼロ・空」の語とつなげています。

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 色の言葉は街でよく目にします。国旗 Jalur Gemilang は赤・白・青・黄色：merah、putih、biru、kuning です。ピンクは merah jambu で、直訳すると「jambu（果物）の赤」です（Kata-Kata カード ms-c05-025）。Yang は複数の中から一つを指します：yang merah は「赤いもの」です（カード ms-c05-004）。

Unit 5 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: マレーシアは一年を通して暑くて湿度が高いので、panas と sejuk は飲み物だけでなく天気の話でも毎日使う言葉です。カウンターでは mahu の代わりに nak をよく聞きます（Saya nak teh tarik）。Kata-Kata は nak を話し言葉としています（カード ms-c05-005）。

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c05 (23 cards, frames ms-c05-f01 and ms-c05-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia "Masak nasi goreng", "Di klinik", "Gambar bayi" and "Lepak di kedai mamak"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 5 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c05-f01, ms-c05-f02, ms-c05-f03, ms-c05-f04, ms-c05-f05 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can describe food, drink, colours, sizes and feelings with an adjective after the noun.
0–5 Recall: chapter 4 (Sudah makan?, the time, a weekly habit) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 to 5, question and answer first, rule second; teach the six word groups across Blocks A to C (not all in one sitting).
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask Bagaimana …? and Kenapa …? and answer with an adjective, tetapi or sebab.
0–5 Recall: colours in the room: Warna apa? round the class.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a short talk about a weekend and use a menu to order a drink the way I like it.
0–5 Recall: learners describe one thing they ate this week: taste and temperature.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check adjectives, colours and question words in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 5, including bagaimana and kenapa), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: chapter 6 Kata-Kata set (comparatives); the writing block for unit 5 comes first if time allows.
Goal: I can recognise words for cooking, the clinic, a baby photo and the mamak in four Kata-Kata Dunia scenes.
0–5 Recall: order a drink: sweetness, hot or cold, ice.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Masak nasi goreng", "Di klinik", "Gambar bayi" and "Lepak di kedai mamak" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
30–40 Free variation: the dish is finished, or the friend wants something that is not spicy.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 63 core words in six groups. Route 1 (whole unit): tastes and the question and linking words in Block A; colours, size and shape in Block B; feelings and states, hot, cold, food and drink in Blocks C and D; Block E recycles all of them in the Dunia scenes. Route 2 (A/B in the pilot): split the same plan into two halves, Blocks A and B on tastes, the question and linking words, hot, cold, food and drink and ordering, then Blocks C and D on colours, size and shape and feelings. Note which route needs fewer repeats. The Dunia words are for recognition only.

Standard first: mahu, tetapi, bagaimana. The spoken forms nak, tapi and macam mana are marked spoken; accept them in pair work once the standard form is on the board. jingga and oren are both correct for orange (Sam, 12 Nov 2026).
tidak negates adjectives and verbs; bukan negates nouns (chapter 3). Ask: "Is it a noun or a description?"
No comparatives or superlatives (chapter 6): do not teach lebih, paling or kurang … daripada. kurang manis is a fixed ordering phrase only.

Unit 5 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: rasa is a noun (taste: Bagaimana rasa …?) and a verb (to feel: Saya rasa penat.). Kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab are equivalents (Sam, 12 Nov 2026); answer with sebab or kerana, mainly. Use kenapa in everyday talk and let learners hear mengapa as the same question. tawar is "bland" here; learners met it as "to bargain" in chapter 3. seronok and tawar were recognition words earlier and are core here because the ledger places them in chapter 5.

Clinic scene: symptoms only (demam, batuk, sakit kepala, perut, tekak). Do not teach diagnoses, medicines or doses. hospital is the recognition word for the hospital here and a taught word in chapter 7; the Indonesian-leaning rumah sakit is not taught (Sam, 12 Nov 2026).
No food rules or religious expressions are taught in this unit. Ask Sam before adding any. The culture note says who traditionally runs a mamak stall, as Sam approved on 12 Nov 2026.
Dunia words from the four scenes are for recognition in Block E only.

Unit 5 · Writing block · A short descrip.source_text: Part 1 (15 min): choose a drink, a dish or a place you know. Write four to six sentences: colour, size, taste, hot or cold. Use tetapi once and sebab once.
Part 2 (15 min): swap with your partner and read aloud. Your partner asks Bagaimana …? and Kenapa …?.
Part 3 (15 min): rewrite your text after the questions, adding one adjective for colour or size.
パート1：飲み物・料理・場所を選び、4〜6文で描写（色・大きさ・味・温度）。tetapi と sebab を一回ずつ。パート2：交換して音読し、Bagaimana …?・Kenapa …? で質問。パート3：質問を受けて、色か大きさの形容詞を一つ足して書き直す。
☐ Each adjective comes after its noun and does not change.
☐ tidak (not bukan) stands before an adjective.
☐ tetapi joins two contrasting ideas; sebab (or kerana) comes before the reason.
☐ Standard forms (mahu, tetapi) are used in writing; spoken forms are not.
Model: Hari Sabtu saya makan mi goreng di mamak. Mi goreng itu pedas, tetapi sedap. Teh tarik saya sejuk dan kurang manis. Saya kenyang dan gembira sebab makanan sedap.
target_spans: Hari Sabtu saya makan mi goreng di mamak. Mi goreng itu pedas, tetapi sedap. Teh tarik saya sejuk dan kurang manis. Saya kenyang dan gembira sebab makanan sedap.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: (A) lebih (adjective) daripada (B). / (A) kurang (adjective) daripada (B).

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Kondo A lebih besar daripada kondo B? B: Ya, kondo A lebih besar.
target_spans: Kondo A lebih besar daripada kondo B?

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Kondo A atau kondo B lebih mahal? B: Kondo A lebih mahal daripada kondo B.
target_spans: Kondo A atau kondo B lebih mahal?
Kondo A lebih mahal daripada kondo B.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Teh ini lebih manis daripada kopi itu? B: Tidak, teh ini kurang manis.
target_spans: Teh ini lebih manis daripada kopi itu?

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Komputer baru lebih cepat daripada komputer lama? B: Ya, lebih cepat sedikit.
target_spans: Komputer baru lebih cepat daripada komputer lama?

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Hari ini lebih panas daripada semalam? B: Ya, semalam hujan.
target_spans: Hari ini lebih panas daripada semalam?

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 6. A: Soalan ini kurang susah daripada soalan semalam? B: Ya, soalan ini lebih mudah.
target_spans: Soalan ini kurang susah daripada soalan semalam?

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Explanation: lebih goes before the adjective and means "more" or "-er": lebih besar. daripada introduces the thing you compare with: lebih besar daripada kondo B. When both people know the other thing you can leave daripada out: Kondo B lebih murah. kurang before an adjective means "less" or "not so": kurang besar. The adjective itself never changes. sedikit after the adjective makes the difference small: lebih cepat sedikit.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 説明：lebih は形容詞の前に置き「もっと」「〜より」の意味です：lebih besar。daripada は比べる相手を導きます：lebih besar daripada kondo B。相手が分かっていれば daripada は省けます：Kondo B lebih murah. 形容詞の前の kurang は「より少ない・あまり〜ない」：kurang besar。形容詞の形は変わりません。形容詞のあとに sedikit を付けると、差が小さいことを表します：lebih cepat sedikit。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese puts the standard first (Bより大きい). Malay puts it last: A lebih besar daripada B. Japanese adjectives change form (大きい / 大きくない), Malay adjectives never do; lebih and kurang are separate words in front.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は比べる相手を先に言います（Bより大きい）。マレー語は最後です：A lebih besar daripada B。日本語の形容詞は形が変わります（大きい／大きくない）が、マレー語の形容詞は変わらず、lebih と kurang は前に置く別の語です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: Pattern box: (A) sama (adjective) dengan (B). / (A) setinggi (B). / (A) semahal (B).

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 2. A: Anak encik sudah setinggi encik? B: Ya, sekarang dia setinggi saya.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 3. A: Kondo B sama besar dengan kondo C? B: Tidak, kondo C lebih kecil.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 4. A: Pisang hari ini semahal mangga? B: Ya, harga pisang dan mangga sama.
target_spans: Ya, harga pisang dan mangga sama.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: 5. A: Bilik air ini sama bersih dengan bilik air itu? B: Tidak, bilik air itu lebih bersih.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 6. A: Kopi ini sama pahit dengan kopi itu? B: Ya, sama pahit.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Explanation: sama + adjective + dengan says two things are equal, as … as: sama besar dengan kondo C. The adjective sits between sama and dengan. setinggi (as tall as) and semahal (as expensive as) are single ledger words: learn them as whole words. For every other adjective use sama … dengan. Building new words like these is a later chapter, so do not make new ones yet.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：sama + 形容詞 + dengan は「〜と同じくらい〜」です：sama besar dengan kondo C。形容詞は sama と dengan の間に入ります。setinggi（同じくらい高い）と semahal（同じくらい高価）は台帳の一語なので、そのまま覚えます。ほかの形容詞には sama … dengan を使います。この形の新しい語を作るのはあとの章なので、まだ作りません。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese says Bと同じくらい高い: dengan (と) comes last in Malay, after the adjective: sama tinggi dengan B. The whole words setinggi and semahal need no dengan and no sama.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「Bと同じくらい高い」と言います。マレー語の dengan（と）は最後で、形容詞のあとです：sama tinggi dengan B。setinggi と semahal は一語で、sama も dengan も要りません。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: Pattern box: (A) paling (adjective). / (A) termurah / terbesar / terbaik / tercantik.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 1. A: Siapa paling tinggi di pejabat? B: Bos saya paling tinggi.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 2. A: Kondo C paling murah? B: Ya, kondo C termurah.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 3. A: Kondo A paling besar? B: Ya, kondo A terbesar.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 4. A: Kondo D terbaik? B: Ya, kondo D yang terbaik.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 5. A: Pantai di pulau itu cantik? B: Cantik sekali! Itu pantai yang tercantik.
target_spans: Cantik sekali! Itu pantai yang tercantik.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 6. A: Bila stesen paling ramai? B: Pukul lapan pagi stesen paling ramai.
target_spans: Pukul lapan pagi stesen paling ramai.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Explanation: paling before any adjective means "the most": paling murah, paling ramai. Four ledger words say the same in one word: termurah (cheapest), terbesar (biggest), terbaik (best), tercantik (most beautiful). Learn these four as whole words. paling is the way to make the rest. yang terbaik means "the best one".

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 説明：paling は形容詞の前に付いて「一番〜」の意味です：paling murah、paling ramai。台帳には一語で同じ意味の語が四つあります：termurah（一番安い）、terbesar（一番大きい）、terbaik（一番良い）、tercantik（一番きれい）。この四つは一語としてそのまま覚えます。ほかは paling で作ります。yang terbaik は「一番良いもの」です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 一番 is also a word in front of the adjective (一番安い = paling murah), so the order matches. termurah is one word, like 最安.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「一番」も形容詞の前に来るので、語順は同じです（一番安い＝paling murah）。termurah は「最安」のような一語です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: Pattern box: Yang mana (lebih) ___ ? / (noun) yang mana? / Saya pilih yang ___ .

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 2. A: Encik suka kondo yang mana? B: Saya suka kondo yang baru.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: 3. A: Yang mana encik pilih? B: Saya pilih yang ini.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 5. A: Komputer yang mana lebih cepat? B: Yang baru.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 6. A: Yang mana paling murah? B: Yang itu paling murah.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: Explanation: yang mana means "which one" and stands where the answer will stand: Yang mana lebih selesa? Kondo D. After a noun it means "which …": kondo yang mana. pilih is "to choose": Saya pilih yang ini. lain means "other": Ada kondo lain? yang ini is "this one", yang itu is "that one".

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 説明：yang mana は「どれ」で、答えが入る位置に置きます：Yang mana lebih selesa? Kondo D. 名詞のあとでは「どの〜」：kondo yang mana。pilih は「選ぶ」：Saya pilih yang ini. lain は「他の」：Ada kondo lain? yang ini は「これ」、yang itu は「それ」です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese separates どれ (three or more) from どちら (two); Malay uses yang mana for both. pilih is one plain verb, like 選ぶ.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語はどれ（3つ以上）とどちら（2つ）を使い分けますが、マレー語はどちらも yang mana です。pilih は「選ぶ」にあたる普通の動詞です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|15.source_text: 1. A: Kondo ini selesa? B: Ya, sangat selesa.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|16.source_text: 2. A: Kafe itu bising? B: Ya, bising sekali.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|17.source_text: 3. A: Mi goreng ini pedas? B: Terlalu pedas untuk saya.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|18.source_text: 4. A: Bagaimana pantai itu? B: Cantik sekali!

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|19.source_text: 5. A: Encik suka kondo C? B: Tidak. Kondo C terlalu kecil.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|20.source_text: 6. A: Bagaimana pejabat baru? B: Pejabat baru amat selesa.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|21.source_text: Explanation: sangat goes before an adjective and means "very": sangat selesa. sekali goes after it and means the same: bising sekali. amat is also "very", but formal. terlalu means "too": more than is good. Compare sangat panas (very hot) with terlalu panas (too hot to enjoy).

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: 説明：sangat は形容詞の前に置き「とても」：sangat selesa。sekali は形容詞のあとに置いて同じ意味です：bising sekali。amat も「とても」ですが、改まった言い方です。terlalu は「〜すぎる」で、よくない程度を表します。sangat panas（とても暑い）と terlalu panas（暑すぎる）を比べましょう。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: 「暑すぎる」has すぎる attached to the adjective stem; in Malay terlalu is a separate word in front, and the adjective does not change: terlalu panas. とても ≈ sangat.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：「暑すぎる」は形容詞の語幹に「すぎる」が付きますが、マレー語の terlalu は前に置く別の語で、形容詞は変わりません：terlalu panas。とても ≈ sangat です。

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|3.source_text: Pattern 2: setinggi and semahal are whole words. If a learner invents another word of this kind, say it is understood but ask for sama besar dengan instead; the building rule comes later.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|4.source_text: Pattern 3: paling murah and termurah mean the same. Accept either; only the four ledger words are taught as whole words.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|5.source_text: Pattern 4: yang mana stands where the answer will stand; learners answer with the noun or with yang ini / yang itu.

Unit 6 · Pattern and grammar focus|7|6.source_text: Pattern 5: terlalu is the one that carries a complaint; sangat does not. Ask: "Is it good or a problem?"

1. Ask a colleague how they are. (apa)

6. Ask the price of the condo. (berapa)

11. Ask why a colleague does not like condo C. (kenapa; also mengapa or apa sebab; the answer starts with sebab or kerana)
12. Ask a friend which condo they like. (yang mana)

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Kondo is the everyday Malaysian word for a condominium: a block of homes with shared areas. It is a headword in Kamus Dewan (the ledger's check). The owners of a condominium together form a management body that looks after the shared areas, under Malaysia's Strata Management Act 2013, so talking about a kondo often means talking about the whole building too: is it bersih, sunyi or bising?

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: The Klang Valley, the urban area around Kuala Lumpur, has a rail network that includes LRT, MRT, monorail and KTM Komuter lines, so stesen is a word you read on signs and hear on the platform. When you say where you live or work, a station is an easy thing to describe: Stesen sangat ramai pukul lapan.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Kata-Kata's card notes show how some comparing words are made. setinggi is se- + tinggi and semahal is se- + mahal; terbaik comes from baik with ter-. Learn them as whole words for now. For other adjectives, say sama … dengan or paling. bersih is a root word that only looks like a ber- word.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: Two small words change meaning. After an adjective, sekali means "very" (cantik sekali); it is the same word as "once" in chapter 4. baru is "new" here and "just" in chapter 4. In the Kata-Kata scene the agent says Kondo B kurang besar: kurang with an adjective means "less" or "not so".

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: Kondo は、マレーシアで日常的に使う「コンドミニアム」の言葉で、共用部分のある集合住宅を指します。Kamus Dewan に見出し語として載っています（台帳の確認）。コンドミニアムの所有者はみなで管理組合をつくり、共用部分の世話をします。これはマレーシアの Strata Management Act 2013 に基づいています。そのため kondo の話は建物全体の話にもなりがちです：bersih か、sunyi か、bising か。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: クランバレー（クアラルンプール周辺の都市圏）には LRT、MRT、モノレール、KTM Komuter などの鉄道網があるので、stesen は標識で目にし、ホームで耳にする言葉です。住んでいる場所や職場を話すとき、駅は説明しやすい題材です：Stesen sangat ramai pukul lapan.

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記から、比べる言葉のでき方が分かります。setinggi は se- + tinggi、semahal は se- + mahal で、terbaik は baik に ter- が付いた形です。今は一語としてそのまま覚えましょう。ほかの形容詞には sama … dengan か paling を使います。bersih は接頭辞の付いた語に見えるだけの、語根の単語です。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: 二つの小さな語は意味が変わります。形容詞のあとの sekali は「とても」の意味です（cantik sekali）。第4章の「一度」と同じ語です。baru はここでは「新しい」、第4章では「〜したばかり」です。Kata-Kata の場面で不動産担当者は Kondo B kurang besar と言います。形容詞の前の kurang は「より少ない」「あまり〜ない」の意味です。

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: English note: 228 words. The Japanese is a full translation (draft).

Unit 6 · Culture and usage note|4|1.source_text: Sources: Kata-Kata chapter 6 cards ms-c06-005, -006, -008, -014, -021 and -031 (notes: se- + tinggi, se- + mahal, cantik sekali, baik → terbaik, baru, a root word that only looks like a ber- word) and scenario ms-c06-s01 to s08; ledger L-0294 (kondo, KD4 check "Headword"); Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757): Wikipedia, "Strata Management Act 2013", and the municipal pages on joint management bodies and management corporations (MBSA and MBS) seen in a search summary; the Act itself was not opened (Rank 3, one Rank 2 local-government page); Klang Valley rail network: Wikipedia, "Klang Valley Integrated Transit System" and "RapidKL" seen in a search summary (Rank 3; line names and opening dates differ between sources, so none is given). The note makes no claim about prices, rents or neighbourhoods; the practice prices are fictional.

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|3|.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c06 (16 cards, frames ms-c06-f01 and ms-c06-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 6 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c06-f01, ms-c06-f02, ms-c06-f03, ms-c06-f04, ms-c06-f05, ms-c06-f06 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can compare two things with lebih or kurang and daripada, and say they are the same with sama … dengan.
0–5 Recall: chapter 5 (taste, hot or cold, Kenapa …? Sebab …) from the opener prompts.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 and 2, question and answer first, rule second; teach the first two word groups and the describing words in Blocks A and B, not all in one sitting.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can say which is the most with paling, use sangat and terlalu, and ask and answer Yang mana …? with pilih.
0–5 Recall: two things in the room: Yang mana lebih besar? round the class.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the markers drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a talk about a new home and use a short listing to choose a condo.
0–5 Recall: learners compare two drinks or two foods from last week: lebih manis, kurang pedas.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|4|.source_text: 30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check comparing words, sangat and terlalu, and place words in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 6, including yang mana), then the markers drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: chapter 7 Kata-Kata set (places and directions); the review block after unit 6 is not yet written, so use the mixed review from Block D.
Goal: I can recognise words for the game, the court and the body in the Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton" and compare two players.
0–5 Recall: compare two condos with lebih, paling and terlalu.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Main badminton" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
15–30 Role-play of the scene in pairs.
30–40 Free variation: two players compare height and speed (a pair role-play), then they change who wins.
■ What to listen for · 注意点

Load: 32 core words in six groups. Suggested order: Block A the comparing and equal words, paling and the four whole words; Block B sangat, terlalu, choosing words and the describing words; Block C and D recycle them in the condo listing, the listening and the test; Block E recycles the comparing words in "Main badminton". If the pilot shows 32 is too many for one unit, the natural cut is A/B: comparing, equal and most first; very, too, choosing and the describing words second.

sekali and baru were taught in chapter 4 with other meanings (sekali once, baru just). Chapter 6 adds sekali = very after an adjective and baru = new. They are revision with a note (the ledger places them in chapters 4 and 6).

termurah, terbesar, terbaik, tercantik, setinggi and semahal are taught as whole ledger words. Do not drill making new ter- or se- words: productive ter- is chapter 16. paling + adjective is the way to make a new superlative, and sama … dengan the way to say equal.

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|5|.source_text: Standard first: mudah (standard) and senang (spoken) are shown together; accept both. [UNVERIFIED] Whether Kamus Dewan marks senang as spoken is not checked (see the report). senang is also heard in a different meaning ("at ease"); that is not taught here.

The Kata-Kata scene uses dekat, jauh and the abbreviation LRT, which are outside chapters 1 to 6 (dekat and jauh are chapter 7), so the scene here compares size, price, noise, age and comfort. Rents: the word for rent is not in the ledger (proposed in the report); the listing says setiap bulan beside the price. Do not add words from chapter 7 or later to the condo scenes.
terlalu is "too" and carries a complaint; sangat is "very" and does not. amat is the formal "very"; it fits a letter or a speech more than a chat.
"Main badminton" is for recognition. The body words (lengan, bahu, siku, lutut, pinggang) are labels in a sports scene: no injuries, advice or medicine. kurang before a noun is not taught.
Cumulative question words now include yang mana (chapters 1 to 6). Chapter 5 words bagaimana and kenapa (= mengapa = apa sebab, answered with sebab or kerana) return in drill 5 and in the listening.

Unit 6 · Teaching plan and answer key|6|.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. No productive ber- or me- verbs (root verbs only).

Chapter 5 · Fast-course summary pack|4|5.source_text: Remember: the adjective comes after the noun and never changes; tidak goes before an adjective, bukan before a noun. sebab (or kerana) comes before the reason; kenapa, mengapa and apa sebab all mean "why". kurang manis is a fixed ordering phrase; comparing things comes in chapter 6.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|1.source_text: 2 · (A) sama (adjective) dengan (B).  e.g. Kondo D sama mahal dengan kondo A. / Kondo B sama besar dengan kondo C.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|2.source_text: 3 · (A) paling (adjective).  e.g. Kondo C paling murah. / Kondo D yang terbaik.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|3.source_text: 4 · (noun) sangat / terlalu (adjective).  e.g. Kondo D sangat selesa. / Kondo C terlalu bising.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|4.source_text: 5 · Yang mana ___ ?  Saya pilih ___ .  e.g. Yang mana lebih selesa? Kondo D. / Encik pilih yang mana? Saya pilih kondo D.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|5.source_text: Remember: the adjective never changes. lebih, kurang, paling, sangat and terlalu go before it; sekali (very) goes after it. daripada comes after the adjective, before the thing you compare with. terlalu means too much; sangat means very. termurah, terbaik and the other whole words are learned as they are; for other adjectives use paling and sama … dengan.

Chapter 6 · Fast-course summary pack|4|6.source_text: 形容詞は変わりません。lebih・kurang・paling・sangat・terlalu は形容詞の前、sekali（とても）はあとに置きます。daripada は形容詞のあと、比べる相手の前に置きます。terlalu は「〜すぎる」、sangat は「とても」です。termurah・terbaik などの一語はそのまま覚え、ほかの形容詞には paling と sama … dengan を使います。
